title: Receipted delivery: explicit attempt ownership and transfer state, so pruning can settle only a positively known-untransferred attempt
outcome: Receipted delivery: explicit attempt ownership and transfer state, so pruning can settle only a positively known-untransferred attempt
acceptance: Every promoted receipted attempt carries an explicit ownership and transfer state, initialized before the attempt is exposed and updated atomically before its dispatch carrier is handed out (the immediate dispatch, a parked or deferred carrier, or a retained queued admission)

Pruning may reject only a positively known-untransferred attempt whose executable carriers have been revoked; missing, old, restored or default ownership evidence stays unresolved or Ambiguous and is never read as a rejection

The guard backs up the explicit settlements at each known retirement and discard site and replaces none of them; tests show a restart with old state never infers a rejection and never authorizes a second delivery
